questions: Should the random seed be set only for generating the sample data (if needed) or also for any internal randomness in matplotlib's histogram binning or other plotting steps?

If the attribute values are all identical (e.g., all 5), how should the histogram bins be defined? Should it use a single bin covering the single value, or default bin edges that might produce empty bins?
Should the histogram include edge color, fill color, or other stylistic properties beyond alpha=0.5, or are those left to matplotlib defaults?
Is the 'seed' parameter intended to control randomness in the Object initialization when value is None, or also for any other random operations within the function?
What should happen if the attribute specified by 'attr' does not exist on some or all objects in obj_list? Should the function raise an error, skip those objects, or use a default value?
Should the histogram bins be aligned to integer boundaries or follow matplotlib's automatic bin edges, which might produce fractional boundaries?
Is the function expected to display the plot (e.g., via plt.show()) or only return the Axes object without displaying?
Should the histogram normalize the counts (density=True) or show absolute counts (default)?
